results.text:
extreme poverty in 2020, poverty rates began to decline, though at a slower pace than previously.

Had poverty continued to decline at the pace observed between 2000 and 2013, the extreme poverty rate would have reached roughly 7 percent by 2026, some 3 percentage points below the actual rate (refer to figure 1.1). In absolute terms, this gap represents approximately 240 million more people living in extreme poverty than would have been the case under the earlier trajectory of poverty reduction. The slowdown relative to the 2000–13 trend is only observable at the $3.00 line. At the higher poverty lines (for example, $4.20), actual poverty reduction has broadly kept pace with the pre-2013 trend.
